description: Valid SLDS component composition patterns for structural validation

patterns.notes: Atomic action control. Only supporting visuals such as icons or a loading spinner should be nested.
Use for grouped actions with shared spacing and alignment.
Card is a flexible surface. Keep child composition shallow and use slots/regions consistently.
Atomic checkbox control. Do not nest additional SLDS controls inside the checkbox.
A checkbox group should contain only related sl-checkbox options.
Modal container for short tasks, confirmations, and focused flows.
Side-sheet container suited to contextual editing and more spacious overlays.
sl-form wraps labeled fields, optional form-level feedback, and action groups.
Each form-field should wrap one control or one control-group plus its label, hint, and validation state.
Standalone visual primitive with no structural child relationship.
Inline feedback can include one action or a compact action group.
sl-menu owns a list of menu items. Keep non-item content outside unless you are intentionally building custom menu chrome.
Menu items may include decorative/supporting elements and can host a submenu where supported.
Use sl-menu-button as the trigger/container for a menu, optionally with an icon in the trigger.
Popover hosts lightweight anchored content. If the content becomes application-level, consider dialog or drawer instead.
Progress bar is a leaf component that should not contain nested SLDS children.
Atomic radio control; related options should be grouped by sl-radio-group.
A radio group should contain only mutually exclusive sl-radio options.
Select options must be declared as sl-option children.
Option rows may include an icon, but they should not wrap other interactive components.
Loading placeholder component with no meaningful children.
Spinner is a standalone status indicator.
Atomic binary setting control.
Tabs require both triggers and panels in a coordinated one-to-one structure.
Tab trigger may include an icon or badge alongside its label.
Panels host the actual content for each tab and can contain higher-level page building blocks.
Text field may expose prefix/suffix icon composition only.
Textarea is a leaf input and should not contain SLDS children.
Toggle button behaves like a button with state; only supporting visuals should be nested.
Toggle group should contain only toggle buttons.
Tooltip content is text or lightweight markup; treat it as a leaf in SLDS-only nesting validation.
Avatar may fall back to an icon when no image or initials are available.
Badges may include a compact icon, but avoid turning them into complex containers.
Breadcrumbs usually contain links/text rather than other SLDS components from this rule set.
Data grid structure is primarily API/configuration-driven rather than nested SLDS child components.
Paginator is a standalone navigation control, usually placed next to or below other content.
Search field may include supporting icon composition but should otherwise stay atomic.
Tags can host compact leading visuals such as an icon or avatar.
Tag list should contain sl-tag items only.
Accordion groups collapsible sections. Compose content through sl-accordion-item children.
Accordion items contain the actual content for each collapsible section.
Calendar is a self-contained date browsing and selection surface.
Callout can include supporting actions or an icon, but keep the message content concise.
Combobox manages its text entry and popup suggestion behavior internally.
Date field is an atomic input control for date values.
Editor owns its internal editing surface; surround it with external layout or toolbars instead of nesting SLDS children inside.
Format-date is a read-only formatting primitive.
Format-number is a read-only formatting primitive.
Infotip is a lightweight help surface and should be treated as a leaf component.
Listbox should contain options or grouped options only.
Option groups organize related listbox options under a shared heading.
Message dialog is a focused overlay for short descriptive content and a compact set of actions.
Number field is an atomic numeric input control.
Panel is a flexible surface for grouped content, forms, or structured data.
Time field is an atomic input control for time values.
Toolbar groups closely related actions, filters, and lightweight controls in one horizontal command region.
Toolbar divider is a structural separator and should not contain nested content.
Tree manages hierarchical nodes internally and should be treated as a leaf at the page-composition level.

antiPatterns.reason: Nested interactive elements violate accessibility rules and create conflicting click targets.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Use sl-button-bar for grouped actions or place the secondary action beside the primary button.

antiPatterns.pattern: Multiple input controls inside one sl-form-field
antiPatterns.reason: Labels, hints, and validation messages become ambiguous when one field wraps several unrelated controls.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Create one sl-form-field per control or use a proper group component such as sl-checkbox-group or sl-radio-group.

antiPatterns.reason: Options are only meaningful in the context of a select control.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Move the option under sl-select or switch to sl-menu/sl-menu-item for freeform action lists.

antiPatterns.pattern: Standalone sl-radio elements used as a checklist
antiPatterns.reason: Radios imply mutual exclusivity and should be grouped semantically.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Wrap related radios in sl-radio-group, or use sl-checkbox/sl-checkbox-group for multi-select choices.

antiPatterns.reason: Checkbox and radio semantics conflict and confuse assistive technologies.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Use sl-checkbox inside sl-checkbox-group or replace the container with sl-radio-group.

antiPatterns.pattern: Mismatched counts of sl-tab and sl-tab-panel in one sl-tab-group
antiPatterns.reason: Tabs and panels must map one-to-one for keyboard navigation and screen reader labeling to work correctly.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Keep the number and order of tabs and panels synchronized.

antiPatterns.reason: A menu item is already an interactive command surface; nested controls create broken focus and activation behavior.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Represent the action directly as a menu item, or move complex controls into a popover/dialog.

antiPatterns.pattern: sl-tooltip used as the only label for a form control
antiPatterns.reason: Tooltips are supplemental and may not be discoverable on touch devices or by keyboard/screen-reader users.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Use sl-form-field for the primary label and keep the tooltip for optional extra help.

antiPatterns.pattern: Nested overlays such as sl-dialog inside sl-dialog or sl-drawer inside sl-drawer
antiPatterns.reason: Stacked overlays make focus management, escape behavior, and user orientation fragile.
antiPatterns.suggestion: Use a single overlay with progressive disclosure, tabs, or step-based content.

layoutPatterns.name: Form layout
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-300) gap between fields and var(--sl-size-500) before actions
layoutPatterns.notes: Standard data-entry layout. Fields stack vertically and actions align as one grouped footer.

layoutPatterns.name: Validated form
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-300) between message and first field, then var(--sl-size-300) between fields
layoutPatterns.notes: Use when the form needs top-level status or submit feedback above the fields.

layoutPatterns.name: Confirmation dialog
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-400) content padding with var(--sl-size-300) between message and actions
layoutPatterns.notes: Best for short confirm/cancel flows, optionally with an sl-inline-message for destructive context.

layoutPatterns.name: Drawer edit flow
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-400) vertical spacing in the drawer body
layoutPatterns.notes: Use a drawer for side-by-side editing without fully interrupting the page context.

layoutPatterns.name: Searchable data listing
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-300) within the toolbar and var(--sl-size-400) between toolbar, grid, and paginator
layoutPatterns.notes: Typical list-management page with search, active filters, overflow actions, a data grid, and pagination.

layoutPatterns.name: Tabbed workspace
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-400) between high-level sections inside each panel
layoutPatterns.notes: Use tabs for parallel views that share a page context but differ in underlying content blocks.

layoutPatterns.name: Profile summary card
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-300) between header elements and var(--sl-size-400) between card regions
layoutPatterns.notes: Good for user, teacher, or product summary panels with identity, status, and quick actions.

layoutPatterns.name: Filter bar
layoutPatterns.notes: Supports faceted filtering where selected filters are surfaced as removable tags.

layoutPatterns.name: Overflow action menu
layoutPatterns.spacing: Compact menu item spacing controlled by the menu itself
layoutPatterns.notes: Use for secondary actions that should not take permanent space in the main layout.

layoutPatterns.name: Loading surface
layoutPatterns.spacing: Match the final layout spacing so loading and loaded states occupy similar space
layoutPatterns.notes: Prefer skeletons for content placeholders and sl-spinner for indefinite blocking operations.

layoutPatterns.name: Breadcrumb page header
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-200) between breadcrumbs and the page title region, then var(--sl-size-400) before the primary content
layoutPatterns.notes: Use breadcrumbs above the main page content to show hierarchy and provide quick backtracking.

layoutPatterns.name: Toolbar command row
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-200) to var(--sl-size-300) between toolbar items with var(--sl-size-400) below the toolbar
layoutPatterns.notes: Use for command-heavy views where primary actions, filters, and overflow actions should stay aligned in one row.

layoutPatterns.name: Paginated data set
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-300) within the toolbar and var(--sl-size-400) between toolbar, results, and paginator
layoutPatterns.notes: Common pattern for searchable, pageable data views or result lists.

layoutPatterns.name: Accordion sections
layoutPatterns.spacing: Use the accordion item rhythm and keep var(--sl-size-300) to var(--sl-size-400) inside each expanded section
layoutPatterns.notes: Best for progressive disclosure when the page contains multiple related sections that should collapse independently.

layoutPatterns.name: Tabs page sections
layoutPatterns.spacing: var(--sl-size-400) between major content blocks inside each tab panel
layoutPatterns.notes: Use tab-group composition for peer sections that share the same page context but need separate panels.
